subject.title: Feature: enrich usage/status JSON with agent, cron, and channel labels

question: Which stable JSON attribution fields should OpenClaw expose for status/usage rows, and what privacy rule should apply to channel targets?
rationale: The request would turn currently internal session, cron, and delivery metadata into a public machine-readable contract, so automation should not choose the schema or privacy boundary on its own.

options.title: Add Privacy-Safe Optional Fields
options.body: Expose additive optional fields such as sessionKind, cronJobId/name, channel, channelTargetKind, and runtime while omitting or hashing private target identifiers unless an explicit flag is approved.

options.title: Keep Existing Metadata Only
options.body: Document the current status and sessions.usage fields and defer cron/channel target expansion until a broader telemetry contract is designed.

options.title: Scope To Cron Display Work
options.body: Fold only human-readable cron/session labels into #51184 and leave dashboard-grade JSON attribution out of scope for now.

recommendation.title: Add Privacy-Safe Optional Fields
recommendation.body: Expose additive optional fields such as sessionKind, cronJobId/name, channel, channelTargetKind, and runtime while omitting or hashing private target identifiers unless an explicit flag is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has the strongest recent source-history connection to the current status, usage, and shared usage type projections that would carry the stable contract.
